source_text:
Hecks.bluebook "Lifeadelics" do
  vision "Every Experience session on the calendar, and every registration's road from intent to a confirmed, paid seat."
  core

  aggregate "Event" do
    description "One scheduled session of an Experience — Yogadelics, Hikeadelics, and so on — with a price and a seat count."

    identified_by :slug

    value_object "Slug" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("an event has a slug") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "Money" do
      attribute :cents, Integer
      invariant("a price is never negative") { cents >= 0 }
    end

    value_object "EventName" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("an event has a name") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "Capacity" do
      attribute :value, Integer
      invariant("a session needs at least one seat") { value.positive? }
    end

    attribute :slug,     Slug
    attribute :name,     EventName
    attribute :price,    Money
    attribute :capacity, Capacity

    lifecycle :status, default: "open" do
      transition "Close" => "closed", from: "open"
    end

    command "Schedule" do
      role "Organizer"
      goal "Put a new session of an Experience on the calendar"

      attribute :slug,     Slug
      attribute :name,     EventName
      attribute :price,    Money
      attribute :capacity, Capacity

      emits "EventScheduled"
    end

    command "Close" do
      role "Organizer"
      goal "Stop taking new registrations for this session"

      reference_to Event

      given("an open session can be closed") { status == "open" }

      emits "EventClosed"
    end
  end

  # WHAT WAS REGISTERED FOR, not the calendar entry itself, and not
  # whether it's PAID FOR either, not anymore — Event owns the price and
  # capacity; Registration owns WHO is coming; Payments::Payment
  # (embryonaut_bluebooks, vendored — lifeadelics.hecksagon's own
  # uses_embryonaut_bluebook "payments") owns whether money actually
  # arrived. A registration and its payment share ONE reference —
  # `registration_id` IS the Payment's own `reference`, minted once by
  # whoever creates both (adapters/http_server.rb's POST /registrations)
  # — so "is this registration paid for" is answered by asking Payment
  # (`Payment.find(registration.id).status`), never stored here.
  #
  # USED TO TRACK ITS OWN pending/confirmed/declined, with ConfirmReceipt/
  # RejectPayment reached through a PaymentGateway port's own Receive/
  # Decline (RegistrationPaymentReceived/Declined) — removed wholesale,
  # not deprecated: Payment already carries a full settle/refund/dispute
  # lifecycle (Succeed/Fail/Refund/CompleteRefund/DeclineRefund/
  # OpenDispute/WinDispute/Chargeback) this aggregate would otherwise be
  # duplicating one state at a time, permanently behind (no refund
  # tracking here ever existed; Payment's did from day one).
  aggregate "Registration" do
    description "One person's road from intent to attend an Event — who's coming, not whether they've paid (that's Payments::Payment, same reference)."

    identified_by :registration_id

    value_object "RegistrationId" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("a registration is identified") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    # GREW TO MATCH THE REAL INTAKE FORM (badass-coaching.net's own
    # registration-yoga form, the questions asked when registering for
    # a real event) — `medications`/`health_concerns` are the two
    # fields a deployment-time `Privacy::Mark` (this bluebook never
    # states it itself — see lifeadelics.hecksagon's own `uses_framework
    # "Privacy"`) flags PHI; every other field is ordinary intake, not
    # sensitive.
    value_object "Attendee" do
      attribute :first_name,        String
      attribute :last_name,         String
      attribute :email,             String
      attribute :phone,             String
      attribute :news_signup,       TrueClass, default: false
      attribute :previous_sessions, TrueClass
      attribute :first_time,        TrueClass
      attribute :how_heard,         String
      attribute :medications,       String, optional: true
      attribute :health_concerns,   String, optional: true
      attribute :aim,               String
      attribute :notes,             String, optional: true

      invariant("an attendee has a first name") { !first_name.to_s.empty? }
      invariant("an attendee has a last name") { !last_name.to_s.empty? }
      invariant("an attendee has an email") { !email.to_s.empty? }
      invariant("an attendee has a phone number") { !phone.to_s.empty? }
      invariant("an attendee has answered whether they've done sessions before") { !previous_sessions.nil? }
      invariant("an attendee has answered whether this is their first time") { !first_time.nil? }
      invariant("an attendee says how they heard about the event") { !how_heard.to_s.empty? }
      invariant("an attendee says what they hope to get out of attending") { !aim.to_s.empty? }
    end

    reference_to Event, as: :event_slug

    attribute :registration_id, RegistrationId
    attribute :attendee,        Attendee

    command "Request" do
      role "Guest"
      goal "Register intent to attend an Event — the Payment sharing this same reference is what actually tracks payment"

      reference_to Event, as: :event_slug
      attribute :registration_id, RegistrationId
      attribute :attendee,        Attendee

      emits "RegistrationRequested"
    end

    query "Listing" do
      description "Every registration — the admin Users page's event-subscription table."
    end
  end

  # THIS SITE'S OWN LINK TO ITS OWNER'S PAYMENT-PROCESSOR ACCOUNT — one
  # row per tenant (each tenant boots its own copy of this domain in its
  # own schema, so "one row" IS "one per tenant"). Holds only PUBLIC
  # facts about the connected account: which processor, its account
  # reference (Stripe's `acct_...`), test or live, a display name. It NEVER
  # holds a secret — the processor adapter authorizes through the
  # platform's own credentials (adapters/, world settings), so a tenant's
  # own secret key is never something this service, or its operator,
  # ever sees.
  #
  # `processor` is deliberately open-ended, not `one_of` — a new payment
  # adapter is a new folder under adapters/, not a change here.
  #
  # ENABLED IS A STATE, NOT A FLAG: "connected" only records the link;
  # checkout keeps running on the mock adapter until the operator moves it
  # to "enabled" (EnablePayments). Disconnecting from either state pauses
  # registrations (adapters/http_server.rb) — it never falls back to mock.
  aggregate "PaymentConnection" do
    description "This site's link to its owner's payment-processor account — public facts only, never a secret."

    identified_by :slug

    value_object "ConnectionSlug" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("a payment connection has a slug") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "Processor" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("a payment connection names its processor") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "AccountRef" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("a payment connection names the connected account") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "ConnectionMode" do
      attribute :value, String, one_of: ["test", "live"]
      invariant("a connection is test or live") { ["test", "live"].include?(value) }
    end

    value_object "DisplayName" do
      attribute :value, String
      invariant("a connected account has a display name") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    attribute :slug,         ConnectionSlug
    attribute :processor,    Processor
    attribute :account_ref,  AccountRef
    attribute :mode,         ConnectionMode
    attribute :display_name, DisplayName

    lifecycle :status, default: "connected" do
      transition "EnablePayments"  => "enabled",      from: "connected"
      transition "DisablePayments" => "connected",    from: "enabled"
      transition "Disconnect"      => "disconnected", from: "connected"
      transition "Reconnect"       => "connected",    from: "disconnected"
      transition "Suspend"         => "paused",       from: "enabled"
      transition "Resume"          => "enabled",      from: "paused"
    end

    command "Connect" do
      role "Owner"
      goal "Link this site to its owner's payment-processor account"

      attribute :slug,         ConnectionSlug
      attribute :processor,    Processor
      attribute :account_ref,  AccountRef
      attribute :mode,         ConnectionMode
      attribute :display_name, DisplayName

      emits "PaymentAccountConnected"
    end

    command "Reconnect" do
      role "Owner"
      goal "Link a previously disconnected site to a payment-processor account again"

      reference_to PaymentConnection
      attribute :processor,    Processor
      attribute :account_ref,  AccountRef
      attribute :mode,         ConnectionMode
      attribute :display_name, DisplayName

      given("only a disconnected link can be reconnected") { status == "disconnected" }

      sets :processor
      sets :account_ref
      sets :mode
      sets :display_name

      emits "PaymentAccountReconnected"
    end

    command "Disconnect" do
      role "Owner"
      goal "Unlink this site from its payment-processor account while no real payments are being taken"

      reference_to PaymentConnection

      given("only a connected, not-yet-enabled link can be disconnected") { status == "connected" }

      emits "PaymentAccountDisconnected"
    end

    # DISCONNECTING WHILE PAYMENTS ARE ENABLED IS NOT A PLAIN DISCONNECT —
    # real guests have been paying through this account, so registrations
    # PAUSE (adapters/http_server.rb answers 503) instead of quietly falling
    # back to the mock adapter's fake payment page. Also what a processor's
    # own "access revoked" webhook dispatches.
    command "Suspend" do
      role "Owner"
      goal "Pause registrations because the payment account behind enabled payments is gone"

      reference_to PaymentConnection

      given("only enabled payments can be suspended") { status == "enabled" }

      emits "PaymentsSuspended"
    end

    command "Resume" do
      role "Owner"
      goal "Bring paused payments back by connecting a payment-processor account again"

      reference_to PaymentConnection
      attribute :processor,    Processor
      attribute :account_ref,  AccountRef
      attribute :mode,         ConnectionMode
      attribute :display_name, DisplayName

      given("only paused payments can be resumed") { status == "paused" }

      sets :processor
      sets :account_ref
      sets :mode
      sets :display_name

      emits "PaymentsResumed"
    end

    command "EnablePayments" do
      role "Operator"
      goal "Let checkout take real payments through the connected account"

      reference_to PaymentConnection

      given("payments can only be enabled on a connected account") { status == "connected" }

      emits "PaymentsEnabled"
    end

    command "DisablePayments" do
      role "Operator"
      goal "Stop taking real payments; checkout goes back to the mock adapter"

      reference_to PaymentConnection

      given("only enabled payments can be disabled") { status == "enabled" }

      emits "PaymentsDisabled"
    end
  end
end
